Step 1:

#### Run Setup ####
    chmod +x setup.sh 
    ./setup

#### Verify IAM role attachment ####
    aws sts get-caller-identity


Step 2:

#### Change Directory ####
    cd ~/MCPOpsAgent

#### Project Generation ####
    agentcore create

Step 3:

curl -X POST <<Lambda Public URL>> -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "tools/list", "params": {}, "id": 1}'


Step 4:

#### Move into the automatically generated directory using ####
    cd ~/MCPOpsAgent/myMCPOpsAgentProj/

#### Open and adjust your regional environment targets map using ####
    nano agentcore/aws-targets.json 

#### Open the agent definition file located in the application directory ####
	nano app/myMCPOpsAgentHar/harness.json


Step 5:

#### Clear any local build database artifacts to ensure a clean sync run using ####
	rm -rf .cli/rm -rf cdk.out/rm -f agentcore/.agentcore

#### Execute the native deployment command directly from the project directory using ####
	agentcore deploy


Step 6:
#### Test Agent ####

Code Interpreter — shows sandboxed Python execution:
    agentcore invoke --prompt "Generate a Fibonacci sequence up to 100 and plot it as a bar chart"
    agentcore invoke --prompt "Calculate the standard deviation of [4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42]"


Browser — shows web automation:
    agentcore invoke --prompt "Go to https://aws.amazon.com and tell me the main headline on the page"
    agentcore invoke --prompt "Search for the current AWS re:Invent date on the web and summarize what you find"


Serverless MCP Tool
agentcore invoke --prompt "Get live cluster metrics"


Step 7:

#### Remove All Resources ####
This single command tears down everything that was provisioned during deployment:
agentcore remove all  

Confirm Removal. Once the command completes, confirm everything was torn down successfully:
agentcore list
